rationale: Contract-stability lens over 482bcd2f. The delivered protocol is fundamentally sound and the flagship #186/#233 guarantee is mechanically real: I traced AC-6 end to end — in runMaterialization (materialize.go) both content gates run at lines 208-220 against the snapshot tree, the first MaterializeStageCommit/AdvanceBranchExpectedOld is at lines 233-240, so a doc-sync or ADR refusal exits with zero complete-authored commits; leg (i) pins tip-unchanged-across-refusal in real git; the retry's panel gate then reads tip == ReviewedHeadSHA and doc-sync decides. Reconcile mode is genuinely behavior-untouched: its call path is runCommittedRangeGate -> ValidateDocsRange/CheckADRDivergence, which now delegate to a shared impl with an empty snapshotWorktree sentinel reproducing the pre-bead-6 ChangedFiles leg exactly; runMaterialization is skipped when reconcile != nil, and the orphaned-marker clear (complete.go:750) matches round-4 G1.3. Bead-5's step-6.5 interaction is clean: the indeterminate advanceState return (complete.go:1255-1258) exits before step 6.5, completeSyncPhase runs only when nextMode != "", and the materialization machinery sits entirely upstream of advanceState — bead-5's AC-4/AC-4b tests are unmodified in the diff. The write-ahead resume's panel-gate skip is sound (a marker exists only after every gate passed). HOWEVER, four concrete gaps: (1) deviation C's residual window — the pre-S classification (materialize.go:276) and the S snapshot (materialize.go:292) are separate operations, and a worktree mutation landing between them is staged by the S snapshot's add -A into tree2, committed into D, and — because after the ref advance + index reset the worktree matches D — the sExitContract defensive re-check sees a CLEAN tree and is structurally incapable of catching it. The mutation is silently merged inside a complete-authored commit no gate measured, violating the plan's 'interval edits preserved-or-refused, never silently committed' invariant in the live-race case (deviation C fully fixes the at-rest/kill-window cases legs viii-a/ix pinned, but not this one). A mechanical closure exists and is cheap: refuse before building D unless changedFromCurrent (already computed at line 296) is a subset of materializedArtifactPaths — by construction the only legitimate C->tree2 delta IS the artifact refresh, so any other path is definitionally a swept mutation. This also fully discharges deviation B's coupling (D provably artifact-only without the ninth seam). (2) ADR-0041 does not describe the delivered ordering: sect.1 line 114-116 ('with a final S-exit dirt re-classification') and sect.3(i) line 341-342 ('build commit D, then the S-exit dirt contract') both still describe the plan's original check-AFTER-D ordering — the exact ordering the implementer's own legs proved unsafe. The primary enforcement point (classification BEFORE the D snapshot) appears nowhere in the ADR; the doc must describe what ships. (3) The spec's AC-6 composite fixture (passing panel at SHA A + dirty tracker + doc-sync-failing change; run 1 fails doc-sync with tip still A; run 2 with --allow-doc-skew decided by doc-sync, never stale-SHA) is not delivered as a test anywhere — the pieces exist separately (leg (i) tip-pin on the ADR lane without a panel; the mock-level TestRun_DocSyncRefusesBeforeAnyMaterialization; leg (xi) for AC-7(i)) but the two-run retry-convergence assertion with a REGISTERED panel — the spec's flagship falsifiability surface — has no regression pin. Plan sect.Bead-6 step 6 promised exactly this fixture. (4) resolveMaterializationDiscriminator's unreadable-tip branch (materialize.go:71-80) clears the write-ahead marker and proceeds as a normal run when RevParseRef fails — a failed probe treated as a default classification, destroying recovery evidence on a possibly transient error, contradicting both the prompt's hazard fence ('a failed probe is a refusal or an error, never a default') and the protocol's own 'one invocation can never overwrite another's recovery evidence' invariant; it should propagate the error. Deviations: A acceptable (cosmetic; consider preserving the operator message in the commit body, non-blocking); B safe only modulo finding 1 — the subset guard completes it; C correct in design and judged invariant-preserving for every at-rest case, with finding 1 the one residual and finding 2 the doc obligation its own disclosure names.
concrete_changes_required: Close the classification->snapshot sweep window in runMaterialization's S stage: after computing changedFromCurrent (materialize.go:296), refuse with a named-paths sExitGenuineDirtRefusal-style error before building D if any path in changedFromCurrent is outside materializedArtifactPaths. By construction the only legitimate delta between currentTip and tree2 is the named artifact refresh (preUserDirt was empty), so any other path is a mutation that raced the window between the pre-S classification (line 276) and the S snapshot (line 292); today it is committed into D and the post-commit sExitContract re-check then sees a clean worktree and cannot catch it. This guard makes 'D contains only the named artifact set' mechanical and fully discharges deviation B's coupling on deviation C.

ADR-0041 must describe the DELIVERED S-stage ordering (deviation C): sect.1's amended bullet (line 114-116, 'with a final S-exit dirt re-classification that REFUSES...') and sect.3(i)'s S bullet (line 341-342, 'build commit D, then the S-exit dirt contract') both still describe the plan's original check-after-D ordering the implementer empirically rejected. Amend both to state that the primary interval-edit classification runs BEFORE the S-stage snapshot (so a genuine edit refuses rather than being swept into D by the snapshot's own add -A), with the post-D re-check as defensive; extend adr0041_amendment_test.go to pin the new sentence.

Deliver the plan sect.Bead-6 step-6 AC-6 composite fixture as a real-git test: registered passing panel with ReviewedHeadSHA == A, dirty tracker file, doc-sync-failing change; run 1 fails at doc-sync with `git rev-parse` tip asserted still A; run 2 with --allow-doc-skew is decided by doc-sync (succeeds, or fails at doc-sync again), asserted to NOT fail at the panel stale-SHA gate. The pieces exist separately but the spec's flagship two-run retry-convergence assertion currently has no regression pin.

resolveMaterializationDiscriminator (materialize.go:69-80): on a RevParseRef failure for the bead branch tip, propagate the error instead of clearing the marker and proceeding as a normal run — clearing destroys write-ahead recovery evidence on a possibly transient read failure, and the prompt's own hazard fence requires a failed probe to surface as an error, never a default classification.

findings.title: S-stage classification->snapshot race window is swept silently and the defensive re-check is structurally blind to it
findings.detail: A worktree mutation between checkDirtyTreeFn (materialize.go:276) and SnapshotWorktreeTree (materialize.go:292) enters tree2 via add -A, is committed into D, and after AdvanceBranchExpectedOld + ResetIndexToHead the worktree matches D — so sExitContract's re-classification finds a clean tree and can never catch this case (it only catches mutations landing AFTER the snapshot). The swept content merges ungated inside a complete-authored commit. Real hazard class in this repo's multi-agent operation (the recorded sibling-worktree stray-write incidents). Cheap mechanical closure: subset-guard changedFromCurrent against materializedArtifactPaths before building D.

findings.title: ADR-0041 sect.1 and sect.3(i) describe the rejected check-after-D ordering, not the delivered pre-snapshot classification
findings.detail: Both S-stage descriptions ('a final S-exit dirt re-classification', 'build commit D, then the S-exit dirt contract') match the plan's literal ordering that legs (viii-a)/(ix) proved unsafe and deviation C corrected. The delivered primary enforcement point appears nowhere in the amended ADR, so the doc does not describe what ships — the exact obligation the BRIEF's deviation-C entry asks to be judged.

findings.title: AC-6's composite two-run fixture (panel at A, doc-sync refusal, --allow-doc-skew retry never stale-blocked) is not delivered
findings.detail: No test registers a panel, drives run 1 to a doc-sync refusal with tip asserted unchanged, then asserts run 2 with --allow-doc-skew is decided by doc-sync rather than stale-SHA. Leg (i) pins tip-unchanged on the ADR lane without a panel; TestRun_DocSyncRefusesBeforeAnyMaterialization is mock-level ordering; leg (xi) is AC-7(i). The mechanics compose correctly (traced), but the spec's flagship guarantee — what dissolves #233 for future beads — lacks its own red-on-regression pin, which plan step 6 explicitly promised.

findings.title: Discriminator clears the write-ahead marker on an unreadable tip instead of propagating the error
findings.detail: materialize.go:71-80: a RevParseRef failure is treated as foreign-equivalent (clear marker, proceed). On a transient failure this destroys the marker — the sole recovery evidence for an interrupted materialization — and the subsequent normal run then faces a stale real index (R never ran) with no marker to converge it. Violates the hazard fence 'a failed probe is a refusal or an error, never a default' and the no-evidence-overwrite invariant. Propagate the error.

findings.title: Verified clean: reconcile untouched, bead-5 seam respected, AC-6 mechanics real, resume gate-skip sound
findings.detail: Reconcile path: runCommittedRangeGate -> ValidateDocsRange/CheckADRDivergence with the empty-snapshotWorktree sentinel reproducing pre-bead-6 behavior; runMaterialization never runs in reconcile mode; orphaned markers cleared per round-4 G1.3; terminal clear on both completion paths (complete.go:1157), and a merge failure returns before it so leg-(x) resume evidence survives. Bead-5: the indeterminate return exits before step 6.5; completeSyncPhase guarded by nextMode != ''; no materialization code feeds a phase write. The panel-gate skip on resume is justified — markers publish only after all gates pass. The gate-refusal class is genuinely closed: no complete-authored commit exists before either content gate.

deviations.A: Acceptable. The frozen 4-arg MaterializeStageCommit seam matches the prompt's literal seven-method list; losing the operator's --commit-msg as the materialization subject is an audit-trail cosmetic. Suggest (non-blocking) carrying the operator text in the commit BODY under the Mindspec-Stage trailer in a follow-up — no signature change needed.
deviations.B: The coupling holds only modulo finding R3-1: D-via-full-re-snapshot is safe exactly insofar as the pre-S classification guarantees nothing but the artifact differs, and the classification->snapshot race breaks that guarantee in the live-concurrent case. The changedFromCurrent subset guard (change 1) makes B unconditionally safe without adding the ninth scoped-refresh seam — judged the right resolution.
deviations.C: The design correction is right on the merits: with the check after the S commit, at-rest kill-window edits were provably swept (legs viii-a/ix), and moving the primary classification before the D snapshot preserves the plan's invariant for every at-rest case while keeping the S-exit contract's letter (a genuine edit refuses named, preserved on disk, before any merge). Two obligations remain: the residual live-race window (R3-1, mechanical fix available) and the ADR describing the delivered ordering (R3-2). With changes 1 and 2 landed, deviation C is fully discharged.
